abstract: Fine-mapping methods based on summary statistics from genome-wide association studies and linkage disequilibrium (LD) information are widely used to identify potential causal variants. However, LD mismatch between the external LD reference panel and the genome-wide association study population is common and can compromise fine-mapping accuracy. Here we developed Robust SparsePro (RSparsePro), a probabilistic graphical model with an efficient variational inference algorithm, to perform robust fine-mapping in the presence of LD mismatch. In simulation studies with varying degrees of LD mismatch, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher power and coverage than existing methods. In fine-mapping cis-protein quantitative trait loci and complex trait risk loci, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher enrichment of variants with potential functional impacts and cross-study and cross-LD-reference-panel replication rates. RSparsePro also identified biologically relevant variants in drug target genes and implicated potential regulatory mechanisms for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.
